home.description: Hi, I'm Tomás, though you probably know me as Lewind. I'm a Unity game developer and a full-stack web developer, passionate about creating software that combines creativity, performance, and a solid architecture. I'm currently studying Programming at UTN and dedicate a lot of my time to developing personal projects that allow me to experiment with new technologies, hone my skills, and turn ideas into complete applications and video games.
home.projectsDescription: Here are all the current projects; more will be added over time.

planet-breaker.name: Planet Breaker
planet-breaker.description: A 2D arcade game inspired by Asteroids. You control a spaceship pilot hired by a corporation tasked with destroying the planets of the Federation: an evil organization that has seized control of most of the world's planets. To accomplish this, you'll have access to a vast arsenal of ships, each with different abilities and playstyles.
planet-breaker.objetives: The goal was to create a fast-paced, arcade-style game with a simple movement and shooting system, all focused on the same objective (destroying the planet), but with increasing difficulty as the player progresses. It also offered a straightforward progression system based primarily on skill. While the game is challenging because there's no concept of hit points - if the ship is hit, it dies - this gives the game a more aggressive feel.
features: More than 10 ships with distinct playstyles and abilities.
More than 10 planets with unique abilities.
Permanent and upgradeable progression system using in-game currency.
Variety of enemies: asteroids, enemy ships, satellites, and bosses.
learnings: I understood the importance of Object Pooling for maintaining stable performance in games with a large number of simultaneous enemies and projectiles, reducing the constant creation and destruction of GameObjects.
I learned to design asynchronous loading systems using Addressables, minimizing wait times and improving the player experience through resource preloading.
I developed my own dialogue system based on data files and ScriptableObjects, allowing me to create a flexible, decoupled, and easily extensible solution for events and conversations.
I learned to model relationships between entities using enums and faction systems, achieving complex behaviors such as alliances, neutral enemies, and conflicts between different organizations.
I understood the value of automating repetitive processes. Creating reusable templates for new ships drastically reduced development time and facilitated the addition of content as the project grew.
I gained experience designing persistence systems using JSON files, organizing player progress and configuration. Each ship in a clear, scalable and easy-to-maintain way.
challenges: Optimization was a detail I always kept in mind. Since the enemy generation system is conceptually similar to that of Vampire Survivors, the reuse of GameObjects is crucial to avoid memory and CPU overload. For this, I used a pooling system.

I also aimed for fast loading times. Because the player will be selecting planets very quickly and dying frequently, loading must be as fast as possible. To achieve this, I implemented an asynchronous loading system: the game generates enemies while the player is in the game, and they are pre-loaded before the mission starts since they are all treated as addressable objects.

One challenge was implementing a dialogue system: I wanted to create my own so I could adapt it to my needs. The implementation of this system involves the game loading a text file with the dialogues, and the events are contained in ScriptableObjects. When the corresponding dialogue starts, events are triggered (choosing an option, switching to another dialogue group), all using a dialogue index.

The game includes a war faction system: While it wasn't in the original plans, I decided to implement it. Initially, it had its flaws, as all enemies were considered enemies. However, with the use of enums and types, the enemy's faction will matter significantly, allowing an enemy from faction A to attack faction B. Enemies that act as allies of the player were even implemented.

Another detail I always considered was adding content: Since I'm developing this game alone, time is crucial. At first, it took me quite a while to implement a ship. However, this has been automated, as each ship has its own template of classes and components to fill with data and create the object. What used to take a week now only takes hours, allowing me to add more content quickly.

Implementing a persistence system was also something I had to address: I resorted to using JSON files, as they are much simpler and very easy to read and deserialize as data for the game. Currently, each ship has its own JSON file with its upgrade status and values ​​such as damage and movement speed, in addition to a player file. which determines its general progress (planets destroyed, at what difficulty it destroyed them, etc.)

portfolio.name: Portfolio
portfolio.description: This personal portfolio was developed to showcase my projects, experience, and technical skills. It was designed with a synthwave aesthetic and a scalable architecture that allows for adding new projects, languages, and content without modifying the application's core structure.
portfolio.objetives: The aim was to create a modern, maintainable, and fully scalable web application that serves as a professional presentation and as a platform for documenting development projects.
architecture: Architecture based on Angular Standalone components.
Reusable single page for any project.
Separation of data, presentation, and logic.
Independent services for language and contact.
features: Structure ready for adding new projects without modification.
learnings: Design a reusable architecture for portfolios.
Deploy Angular applications in production with Vercel.
Integrate external services from the frontend.
Design responsive interfaces with a consistent visual identity.
challenges: Design a single page capable of representing any project.
Maintain a structure ready to add new languages.
Integrate EmailJS without requiring a backend.
Achieve a synthwave aesthetic without compromising readability.
Maintain a clean architecture as the project grows.

aboutme.aboutmeDescription: I'm a Unity game developer and a full-stack web developer, passionate about creating software that combines creativity, performance, and a robust architecture. I enjoy transforming ideas into complete projects, designing scalable and reusable solutions that can evolve over time. I'm currently studying Programming at UTN and dedicate a significant amount of my time to developing personal projects to continue learning and refining my skills.
philosophyDescription: I believe that good software should not only work, but also be easy to maintain and evolve. Before implementing any functionality, I strive to understand the problem and design an architecture that allows for component reuse, automates repetitive tasks, and facilitates future expansions. I believe that optimization is only worthwhile when it addresses a genuine need, and that code clarity is just as important as performance.
iLikeDescription: I enjoy creating applications that can grow, focusing more on the system and what it contributes rather than addressing each problem separately.
I enjoy working in a team, learning and listening to different points of view to apply to projects.
aboutme.iResolve: What problems do I enjoy solving?
hobbiesDescription: In my free time I'm a writer; I'm currently working on a science fiction and horror novel. I really enjoy learning about this area because I also use it in video games.
I'm also a Gymrat, I really enjoy exercising and improving my physique, I focus on powerlifting and calisthenics.
I also enjoy playing different video games, and I tend to analyze them and understand how they are made.
objetivesDescription: My goal is to continue growing as a developer by participating in projects that present both technical and creative challenges. I'm interested in working in teams where I can learn from other professionals, contribute well-designed solutions, and continue specializing in both game development and full-stack applications. In the long term, I aspire to develop my own projects with a commercial focus and high quality.
